extracted.intended_audience: writers seeking representation / anyone who may pitch a literary agent in person
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and delivering a tight, well-rehearsed 30-second 'elevator' pitch to a literary agent that introduces you, states your goal, explains why you're the best choice, and ends with a call to action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the literary agent who you are
rubrics_metrics.description: State your name and job title, or the title of the position you’re seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concise and specific. Example: “Hi, my name is Miranda Mechanic, and I’m a licensed automotive mechanic who writes how-to articles for women who don’t want their cars to get the best of them.” This establishes credibility and context in a single sentence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary agents want to know what you want
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t beat around the bush. State what you’re after.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Say your objective plainly (e.g., placement, representation, introduction of a manuscript). Example: “I’m interested in placing some of my articles with your magazine, Auto Care for Everybody.” Clear intent helps the agent decide how to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show the literary agents why you’re the best choice
rubrics_metrics.description: List any degrees, writing credentials, training or experience that relate to what you’re seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only qualifications that match your stated goal. If you lack directly related experience, name relevant qualities or skills (attention to detail, passion, etc.). Keep this brief and focus on the one or two things that set you apart. The page warns: saying you want to write on mechanics but listing degrees in an unrelated field won’t help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give literary agents a call to action
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for what you want to follow up; the call to action leads to further interaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be proactive—invite the agent to see work samples, schedule a meeting, or accept contact info. Example: “I’d like to show you copies of my articles, including ‘How to Change a Tire When It’s Twenty Below Zero’ and ‘How to Add Oil When You’re Wearing a Power Suit.’” The article emphasizes this as a crucial final step: without it you've wasted the pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevity and rehearsal (30 seconds or fewer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to pitch your idea in 30 seconds or fewer (the 'Elevator Pitch'); cultivate a tight, well-rehearsed pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft just a few key sentences and commit them to memory so you never waste an opportunity. The site offers a free download to help fine-tune the pitch. Practice to ensure clarity and timing within the 30-second limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match qualifications to the stated goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the qualifications you cite are relevant to what you’re asking for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid listing unrelated credentials; instead emphasize experience or skills that directly support your request. If no direct credentials exist, state transferable qualities or demonstrable passion. The goal is coherence between your ask and your supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor the pitch to the agent/audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust your pitch for the specific kind of agent or market you’re addressing (New York vs. London, children’s vs. Christian, top-ranking vs. new agents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though the core components remain the same, word choice, examples, and emphasis should reflect the agent’s interests and market. The article implies this by listing different agent types and markets and recommending a few key targeted sentences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confident delivery / take initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver your pitch with confidence and follow through by asking for what you want.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple behavioral guidance: 'Take a deep breath and go for it.' Confidence in delivery helps convert a pitch into further interaction; hesitation or failure to ask for next steps undermines the pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be brief and memorable—find the 'special something'
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for a brief, memorable detail or angle that separates you from the crowd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The key is to be brief and memorable; identify and rehearse that special something that makes your pitch stick in an agent’s mind (a vivid credential, unique experience, or catchy phrasing).
